_readme: Known alternative names, mapping what other datasets call a place to what INEC calls it.
This is DATA, not code, so every language binding gets the same knowledge.
It exists because string similarity cannot reach most of these: 'Yewa North'
is nearest to 'Remo North' (0.67) but is actually Egbado North, renamed in
2020; 'Ado' scores 0.38 against 'Ado Ekiti'; 'Edda' scores 0.22 against its
real target Afikpo South. Each entry below was verified against INEC's list,
Deliberately ABSENT are names that are genuinely ambiguous. A bare 'Ezza'
could be Ezza North or Ezza South; 'Aniocha', 'Oshimili' and 'Afikpo' split
the same way; Edo's 'Central' could be Esan Central or Etsako Central. Those
must come back as ambiguous with candidates, never as a silent guess -- the
resolver handles them by scoring, and adding them here would defeat that.
`target` matches the `name` field exactly. `state` scopes the entry so an
alias can never match across state lines.
